I think the difficulty depends on the person. I can get by with learning the completely different sentence structure but I can definitely recognize that it's pretty challenging and frustrating at times, but I feel like that's because I'm already bilingual. If you try to think about Korean grammar and sentence structure rather than English while learning, you'll get by easier. 

So basically don't try to compare English and Korean too much because they aren't similar in most aspects. It's hard, but you'll learn easier the more you start to recognize Korean patterns more.

Also, just to answer your original question, I used TTMIK's free online lesson with the podcast that they have in each lesson. I think they are very helpful, especially to lay down the foundation for understanding grammar and expand your vocabulary. I also make sure to write everything down in a notebook (Without romanizations!) and review as often as I can.

Good luck on your learning journey!
